items.name: Amazon
facts: Largest river by discharge.
Longest river in South America.
Drains the Amazon rainforest.

items.name: Nile
items.fact: Often cited as the world’s longest river.
facts: Often cited as the world’s longest river.
Flows north through 11 countries.
Empties into the Mediterranean.

items.name: Yangtze
facts: Longest river in Asia.
Called the Chang Jiang in China.
Empties into the East China Sea at Shanghai.

items.name: Mississippi
items.fact: Principal river of the central United States.
facts: Principal river of the central United States.
Runs from Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico.
With the Missouri, among the world’s longest systems.

items.name: Yenisei
items.fact: Great Siberian river flowing to the Arctic.
facts: Great Siberian river flowing to the Arctic.
Among Asia’s longest rivers.

items.name: Yellow River
items.fact: China’s Huang He; “cradle of Chinese civilization.”
facts: China’s Huang He; “cradle of Chinese civilization.”
China’s second-longest river.
Named for the loess silt it carries.

items.name: Ob
facts: Major west Siberian river.
Reaches the Arctic via the Gulf of Ob.

items.name: Paraná
facts: Second-longest river in South America.
Joins the Paraguay and Uruguay in the Río de la Plata.

items.name: Congo
facts: Deepest river; second-largest by discharge.
Africa’s second-longest river.
Forms stretches of the Republic of the Congo–DRC border.

items.name: Amur
items.fact: Border river of China and Russia.
facts: Border river of China and Russia.
Known in China as the Heilong Jiang.
Reaches the Tatar Strait near the Sea of Okhotsk.

items.name: Lena
facts: Great east Siberian river.
Flows to the Laptev Sea in the Arctic.

items.name: Mekong
facts: Major river of Southeast Asia.
Forms stretches of the Laos–Thailand border.
Empties through the Mekong Delta in Vietnam.

items.name: Niger
facts: Principal river of West Africa.
The “Boomerang” river, rising in the Guinea Highlands.

items.name: Murray
facts: Australia’s longest river.
With the Darling, Australia’s main river system.

items.name: Volga
facts: Europe’s longest river.
Empties into the Caspian Sea.

items.name: Ganges
items.fact: Sacred river of the Indian subcontinent.
facts: Sacred river of the Indian subcontinent.
Joins the Brahmaputra in the world’s largest delta.

items.name: Danube
facts: Europe’s second-longest river.
Passes four European capitals.
Europe’s deepest river.

items.name: Indus
facts: Principal river of Pakistan.
Cradle of the Indus Valley civilization.

items.name: Rhine
facts: Major river of Western Europe.
Forms much of the France–Germany border.
Empties into the North Sea in the Netherlands.

items.name: Zambezi
facts: Home of Victoria Falls.
Africa’s fourth-longest river.
Forms stretches of the Zambia–Zimbabwe border.

items.name: Aral Sea
items.fact: Once a great lake; now largely dried.
facts: Once a great lake; now largely dried.
Split between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

items.name: Caspian Sea
items.fact: Largest inland body of water on Earth.
facts: Largest inland body of water on Earth.
A saline lake, not an ocean.

items.name: Lake Baikal
facts: World’s deepest freshwater lake.
Oldest large freshwater lake on Earth.
Holds about one-fifth of the world’s unfrozen fresh water.

items.name: Lake Balkhash
facts: Large endorheic lake in Kazakhstan.
Half fresh, half saline.

items.name: Lake Chad
items.fact: Shallow African lake; size varies greatly.
facts: Shallow African lake; size varies greatly.
Shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger, and Nigeria.

items.name: Lake Erie
facts: Shallowest of the Great Lakes.
Forms part of the U.S.–Canada border.

items.name: Great Bear Lake
facts: Largest lake entirely in Canada.
In the Northwest Territories.

items.name: Great Slave Lake
facts: Deepest lake in North America.
Source of the Mackenzie River.

items.name: Lake Huron
facts: Second-largest Great Lake by area.
Includes Georgian Bay.

items.name: Lake Ladoga
facts: Largest lake in Europe.
In northwestern Russia, near St. Petersburg.

items.name: Lake Malawi
items.fact: Also called Lake Nyasa; African Rift lake.
facts: Also called Lake Nyasa; African Rift lake.
Among the world’s deepest lakes.

items.name: Lake Michigan
items.fact: Only Great Lake entirely in the United States.
facts: Only Great Lake entirely in the United States.
Third-largest Great Lake by area.

items.name: Lake Nicaragua
facts: Largest lake in Central America.
Contains the island of Ometepe.

items.name: Lake Ontario
facts: Easternmost Great Lake.
Drains to the Atlantic via the St. Lawrence.

items.name: Lake Superior
items.fact: Largest freshwater lake by surface area.
facts: Largest freshwater lake by surface area.
Shared by the United States and Canada.

items.name: Lake Tanganyika
facts: Longest freshwater lake; second-deepest.
An African Rift lake shared by four countries.

items.name: Lake Titicaca
facts: Highest large navigable lake; Andes.
Shared by Peru and Bolivia.

items.name: Tonlé Sap
facts: Southeast Asia’s largest freshwater lake.
Swells dramatically in the Mekong flood.

items.name: Lake Victoria
items.fact: Largest lake in Africa by area.
facts: Largest lake in Africa by area.
Source of the White Nile.

items.name: Lake Winnipeg
facts: Large prairie lake in Manitoba.
Twelfth-largest freshwater lake.

items.name: Pacific Ocean
facts: Earth’s largest ocean.
Larger than all of Earth’s land combined.

items.name: Atlantic Ocean
items.fact: Ocean between the Americas, Europe, and Africa.
facts: Ocean between the Americas, Europe, and Africa.
Earth’s second-largest ocean.

items.name: Indian Ocean
items.fact: Ocean between Africa, Asia, and Australia.
facts: Ocean between Africa, Asia, and Australia.
The warmest of the five oceans.

items.name: Arctic Ocean
facts: Smallest and shallowest ocean.
Covered by seasonal sea ice.

items.name: Southern Ocean
facts: Ocean ringing Antarctica.
Defined by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current.

items.name: Mediterranean Sea
items.fact: Sea enclosed by Europe, Africa, and Asia.
facts: Sea enclosed by Europe, Africa, and Asia.
Connected to the Atlantic at Gibraltar.

items.name: Caribbean Sea
facts: Sea of the American tropics.
Bounded by the Antilles and the mainland coasts.

items.name: South China Sea
facts: A major Pacific marginal sea.
Among the world’s busiest shipping lanes.

items.name: Red Sea
items.fact: Narrow sea between Africa and Arabia.
facts: Narrow sea between Africa and Arabia.
Linked to the Mediterranean by the Suez Canal.

items.name: Strait of Gibraltar
items.fact: The Atlantic’s gate to the Mediterranean.
facts: The Atlantic’s gate to the Mediterranean.
Separates Spain from Morocco.

items.name: Bering Strait
facts: Separates Alaska from Russia.
The Pacific’s link to the Arctic Ocean.

items.name: English Channel
facts: Between Great Britain and France.
The Channel Tunnel runs beneath it.

items.name: Drake Passage
items.fact: Open water between South America and Antarctica.
facts: Open water between South America and Antarctica.
The stormiest of the great ocean passages.

items.name: Strait of Malacca
items.fact: Between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.
facts: Between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.
The main shipping choke point of the Indian–Pacific route.

items.name: Gulf of Mexico
items.fact: Atlantic gulf south of the United States.
facts: Atlantic gulf south of the United States.
Fed by the Mississippi River.

items.name: Bay of Bengal
items.fact: Northeastern arm of the Indian Ocean.
facts: Northeastern arm of the Indian Ocean.
The world’s largest bay by area.

items.name: Hudson Bay
items.fact: Huge inland sea of northeastern Canada.
facts: Huge inland sea of northeastern Canada.
Ice-covered for much of the year.

items.name: Persian Gulf
items.fact: Arm of the Indian Ocean between Iran and Arabia.
facts: Arm of the Indian Ocean between Iran and Arabia.
Entered through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.name: Strait of Hormuz
items.fact: The only sea entrance to the Persian Gulf.
facts: The only sea entrance to the Persian Gulf.
A critical oil-shipping choke point.
